claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline, the `SUPERSEDED` execution mode locks a stage so that it processes only one execution at a time.

In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an older execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it ever starts.

In a CodePipeline pipeline using the default `SUPERSEDED` mode, if the CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.

Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each one runs in turn, rather than a later execution superseding an earlier one that never got its turn.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.

When defining a CodePipeline pipeline, both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set to use `QUEUED` execution mode, which can be done with the AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` or `update-pipeline` commands.
The Pulumi AWS provider's `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.

The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is documented at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ and is described further below in the page's 'Manage the pipeline with Pulumi' section.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment, which can be used to prevent concurrent runs of a deployment job that targets that environment.

The link target for the exclusive lock check is the Microsoft Learn page on Azure DevOps Pipelines approvals and checks (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/devops/pipelines/process/approvals?view=azure-devops).
The docs page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and describes Pulumi update conflicts.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a stage-level property that controls how the exclusive lock check on a referenced environment is applied to the stage.
`lockBehavior` in Azure Pipelines accepts the values `sequential` and `runLatest`.
`runLatest` is the default value of the Azure Pipelines stage `lockBehavior` property.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and an older run waiting behind it is passed over (skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time in the same manner as `lockBehavior: sequential`.
`runLatest` is acceptable for a preview environment where only the newest state matters, but not for a stack where every update needs to land.

The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code, documented at /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/.

The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `command: up` running a Pulumi update and `args: --yes` passing the flag through to `pulumi up`; the stack is specified in `org/project/stack` form (`acme/website/production`).
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs target the same Pulumi stack, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.

TeamCity's default behavior is to let a build configuration run concurrently against as many free agents as are available, so nothing in TeamCity prevents concurrent builds of the same configuration from racing on the same stack.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" located under the configuration's General Settings.
The default value of TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" option is 0, which means unlimited.

Setting TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only once the first finishes.

Pulumi Cloud's per-stack update lease gives the same one-at-a-time behavior as limiting TeamCity to one simultaneous build (i.e., concurrent updates to a stack are serialized/only one holds the lease).
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and describes update conflicts.

In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment that the deployment job targets, together with `lockBehavior: sequential` on the stage, serializes Pulumi deployments so they don't run concurrently.
Azure Pipelines supports an 'exclusive lock' check on environments.
Azure Pipelines YAML stages accept a `lockBehavior` setting with the value `sequential`.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section with anchor 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline pipeline execution mode accepts the value `QUEUED`.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section with anchor 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 on the build configuration serializes Pulumi deployments.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section with anchor 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
